أَفْيَحُ A sea, (S, L, K,) and a valley, (Msb,) and any place, (L,) wide, or extensive; (S, L, Msb, K;) as also ↓ فَيَّاحٌ : (S, L, K:) ↓ فَيَّاحٌ occurs in the story of Umm-Zara, accord. to A 'Obeyd, applied to a بَيْت [i. e. house, or tent]; but accord. to others, it is ↓ فَيَاحٌ , without teshdeed: (L:) [the fem. of أَفْيَحُ: and pl. فِيحٌ:] one says دَارٌ فِيْحَآءُ A wide, or an ample, house or abode: (S, K:) and in like manner رَوْضَةٌ [a meadow, &c.]. (L, Msb.) ―
-b2- And فَيْحَآءُ signifies also A sort of thin cooked food, such as is supped, or sipped, (حَسَآءُ,) seasoned with seeds such as are used in cookery. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
